label: Phase 1 restores the deterministic gate: make the two-layer scenario contract explicit (routing precondition, behavior verdict) and rebuild the offline deterministic replay over the existing 28-scenario corpus, gated on the replay first passing against the unchanged hub; risk is scenario-schema churn, mitigated by additive fields with defaults. Classification: NEW.

Phase 2 adds grader self-tests and the honesty rows additively: machine-checkable detection markers with negative fixtures, a review coverage-limits section, a consequence-of-inaction bullet, a report-only lean line, the anti-fabricated-baseline rule and the restraint-counterweight pairing rule; gate is the unchanged exact final-line string plus a green rule-copy canary, with delivery-prefix anchors re-measured if AGENTS.md changes. Classification: NEW.

Phase 3 adds the reuse-evidence step to the always-loaded ladder plus matching removal inventory citations, completes the partially-missing standard-library review row, enumerates the artifact classes to search before calling code unused, and then adds the Lane B size metric as measurement-only with a correctness counterweight; gate is that the always-loaded delivery prefix stays inside the smaller truncation limit, measured before and after, and the metric never gates. Classification: NEW.

Phase 4 is documentation-only: give the retired router-sync check a successor or a named owner, state the external-anchor requirement for agreement guards, and add support-tier plus verified-version rows for runtime surfaces, gated on the drift guards and the commit-time mirror gate still running green. Classification: NEW.

Phase 5 stays deferred: the sk-code surface/standards priming payload needs a named consumer and a delivery-prefix decision, doctrine-effect scenarios need the Phase 1 deterministic layer plus a model-dispatch lane with a control arm, and the subjective shrink row stays out because the lean line carries the information. Classification: NEW.

Phase ordering is gated on measurements rather than preference: Phase 1 establishes the gate that proves later phases do not break routing, Phase 2 changes output contracts that the canary then protects, Phase 3 edits the always-loaded ladder and therefore follows the contract work, Phase 4 runs in parallel as documentation, and no phase claims any size, cost or time saving because no paired baseline exists for the hub's own work. Classification: NEW.

Frontier status: all nine key questions are answered, and four sub-questions stay explicitly unverified rather than claimed — Windows stdin/BOM hook parity, the candidate-arm wiring behind the documented plugin-directory variable, whether a hand-rolled standard-library row exists under unsearched wording, and the current pass state of the design-restraint scenarios whose last verdicts came from a retired harness. Classification: NEW.

Convergence status: rolling new-information ratios were 0.5, 0.31, 0.56, 0.56, 0.69, 0.75, 0.5, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.3, all above the 0.05 threshold because each iteration opened a distinct key question; the honest terminal reason is the 10-iteration cap reached with every key question answered and four sub-questions bounded, not a convergence claim. Classification: NEW.
